title: Uniform finite Tor dimension over an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ in the equivalent small-model derived category [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the canonical geometric stalk rings, module stalks and ring maps of [def-sfb-space-geometric-stalk-models]. Define finite Tor dimension over $Y$ by the uniform geometric-stalk criterion: there is a cochain complex $K$ representing $E$ and integers $a\le b$ such that for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ in the original section universe, every $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, and every geometric point $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ over $s$, the complex $K_x$ restricted along $\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is isomorphic in the module derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to a complex $P_x$ of flat $\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}$-modules with $P_x^n=0$ for $n\notin[a,b]$. No finite generation of the flat terms is required. The same $a,b$ must work for every point, even when $X$ is not quasi-compact. Equivalently, scalar restriction of $E$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$: its derived tensor with every sheaf of $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-modules has cohomology zero outside $[a,b]$. This equivalence is the stalk criterion (Stacks 0DJJ, using enough geometric points of the small etale topos), followed by the bounded-flat-complex criterion (08G1).
